entries.title: C0052 source criterion uses near-critical renormalized coupling
entries.statement: For the zero-field nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic Ising model on Z^3 and beta<beta_c, let U4 be the connected four-point function, chi(beta)=sum_x <sigma_0 sigma_x>, and xi(beta)=[lim_{n to infinity} -(1/n)log<sigma_0 sigma_{n e1}>]^{-1}. Duminil-Copin's Conjecture 6 defines g(beta)=sum_{x2,x3,x4}U4(0,x2,x3,x4)/(chi(beta)^2 xi(beta)^3) and asks that g(beta) not tend to zero as beta increases to beta_c. Since U4<=0, a sufficient equivalent numerical criterion is limsup[-g(beta)]>0. The 4D half of the 2017 conjecture was subsequently proved; current 3D resolution status is not certified by this card.
assumptions: finite susceptibility and exponential correlation length

source.excerpt: If g(beta) tends to 0 as beta approaches beta_c, the field is said to be trivial.

entries.title: Original two-current identity for Ising four-point Ursell function
entries.statement: For a zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model with free boundary conditions on a finite graph, U4(x,y,z,t)=-2 <sigma_x sigma_y><sigma_z sigma_t> P^{xy,zt}[x and z connect in n1+n2], where the two currents are independent with source sets {x} symmetric-difference {y} and {z} symmetric-difference {t}; coincident labels cancel modulo two. The same identity extends to the free infinite-volume state for beta<=beta_c under the source's current-limit conditions. Replacing the original union-current event by clusters enlarged with two independent sourceless currents supplies an upper comparison, not a lower one.
assumptions: finite graph for the direct identity
valid current weak limit for the infinite-volume extension

entries.title: DRAFT C0052 current reduction requires endpoint weights and a near-critical comparison
entries.statement: A statement that 3D Ising nontriviality is equivalent to a uniform intersection probability for two unspecified currents at scale L omits essential data. The exact finite-graph fourth-cumulant identity samples each ordered endpoint pair (x,y) with probability f(x)f(y)<sigma_x sigma_y>/E[(sum f sigma)^2] for nonnegative f, then samples the corresponding original sourced currents. It yields a weighted connection probability. The source's C0052 criterion instead normalizes an infinite-volume beta<beta_c sum by chi(beta)^2 xi(beta)^3. A finite critical block deficit alone does not establish that criterion. W477 L007 supplies a separate exact subcritical sum and a conditional sufficient overlap-ratio bound; that ratio has not been proved bounded. Treat the old unweighted equivalence as a heuristic until the endpoint law and limit comparison are specified.
assumptions: finite-graph weighted identity for nonnegative smearing
no unproved scale-uniform overlap estimate assumed

relations.rationale: The warning compares finite critical block statements with the source's explicit beta<beta_c coupling g(beta).
The warning uses the original two-current U4 identity and its endpoint correlation weights, not the enlarged-event upper comparison.
The existing C0052 concept abbreviates the source criterion; this concept gives the full beta<beta_c g(beta) definition.
The existing private reduction asserts an unweighted inf_L equivalence without specifying endpoint laws or passage to the source's g(beta); this concept records the missing qualifications.
